title: Assessment: Reaction Rates and Energy
description: Checkpoint assessment on reaction-rate factors, energy flow, and real-world control of chemical reactions.

questions.question: Which set lists the four rate factors emphasized in this lesson?
options: Color, odor, mass, and magnetism
Temperature, concentration, surface area, and catalysts
Density, volume, melting point, and boiling point
Gravity, pressure, sound, and light only
questions.explanation: The lesson focuses on temperature, concentration, surface area, and catalysts as major factors affecting reaction rate.

questions.question: A student compares a whole antacid tablet and a crushed antacid tablet in equal amounts of vinegar. Which prediction is best?
options: The crushed tablet reacts faster because it has greater surface area
The whole tablet reacts faster because it has lower surface area
Both must react at exactly the same rate because their mass is similar
Neither can react because vinegar is a liquid
questions.explanation: Crushing increases exposed surface area, allowing more collisions between the tablet and vinegar.

questions.question: True or False: A catalyst speeds up a reaction by being permanently used up as the main reactant.
questions.explanation: False. A catalyst speeds up a reaction but is not consumed overall.

questions.question: Which action is most directly based on lowering temperature to slow reaction rates?
options: Keeping fish on ice after harvest
Crushing a solid into powder
Adding a catalyst to a reactor
Using a more concentrated acid
questions.explanation: Ice lowers temperature and slows many spoilage reactions and microbial processes.

questions.question: A reaction that absorbs energy from the surroundings is called ____.
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions absorb energy from surroundings, which may make the surroundings feel cooler.

questions.question: Burning LPG in a stove releases heat to cook food. This reaction is:
options: endothermic because heat enters the kitchen
exothermic because energy is released to the surroundings
not a chemical reaction because heat is involved
a catalyst because it is useful
questions.explanation: Combustion of LPG is exothermic because it releases energy as heat and light to the surroundings.

questions.question: Explain how lowering concentration can slow a reaction in terms of particle collisions.
questions.correctAnswer: Lower concentration means fewer reactant particles in the same volume, so there are fewer collisions per second and the reaction usually slows down.
questions.explanation: Reaction rate depends partly on collision frequency. Fewer particles per volume usually means fewer effective collisions.

questions.question: True or False: A reaction can be slow and exothermic at the same time.
questions.explanation: True. Rate and energy change are different ideas. A reaction may happen slowly while still releasing energy overall.

questions.question: Which choice best explains why protective paint can help reduce corrosion of a metal gate?
options: It increases the surface area of bare metal
It acts as food for rust
It limits contact between the metal and reactants such as water and oxygen
It makes all corrosion endothermic
questions.explanation: Paint forms a barrier that slows contact between metal and substances involved in corrosion.

questions.question: A student says, 'If a reaction is faster, it must be exothermic.' Correct the statement.
questions.correctAnswer: Fast describes reaction rate, while exothermic describes energy flow. A reaction can be fast or slow and can be exothermic or endothermic depending on whether it releases or absorbs energy.
questions.explanation: Rate and energy change are separate properties. Speed does not automatically tell whether energy is released or absorbed.

questions.question: In manufacturing useful materials, why are catalysts often valuable?
options: They can speed selected reactions without being consumed overall
They always make reactions colder and stop production
They remove the need for reactants
They turn every product into oxygen gas
questions.explanation: Catalysts help reactions proceed faster or under milder conditions and are not used up overall, which can improve efficiency.

questions.question: For a solid reactant, crushing it into smaller pieces increases exposed ____ area.
questions.explanation: Crushing a solid increases surface area, giving more contact between reactants and often increasing reaction rate.
